pr_title: Return the real MAC address for LIFX bulbs with newer firmware
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Avi Miller <me@dje.li>

<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
LIFX introduced a change in firmware 3.70 that resulted in the serial number used by the LIFX LAN protocol no longer being the mac address. This broke the connection between integrations that use MAC address identifiers. This PR fixes that by calculating the correct mac address for bulbs running firmware 3.70 or higher for the bulb's entry in the device registry. 

Also resolves a bug introduced in #58312 which made all LIFX
bulbs get the the model name "True".

pr_comments: This replaces #58457 and addresses the review comments from @frenck. Instead of using `getmac`, I just add 1 to the final octet. This has been tested locally with my collection of 57 LIFX bulbs (which has one of every type) and a range of firmwares.
I think code would be clearer if it was a separate function instead of inside `device_info`, eg.`get_real_mac`
@epenet I have moved the logic to a function but I'm OK to pick up your PR in a rebase, if necessary.
Thanks for the review. Changes tested locally and applied.

issue_context.title: LIFX bulbs with firmware 3.70 (or higher) now have different serial/MAC addresses
issue_context.body:
### The problem

From [this post on Reddit from `u/lifx`](https://www.reddit.com/r/lifx/comments/pb9hbe/comment/hahsyp7/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web2x&context=3):

> There has been a changed in the low level MAC address reported from v3.70 onwards. This is the MAC address reported to the router and will now be the MAC printed on the bulb + 1.
The MAC used in the SSID and reported via the protocol and used in the App remains the MAC printed on the bulb, i.e. no change.
This means that if you had static IP addresses configured prior to v3.70 you would need to update these in your router.
For FW < 3.70:- Printed MAC as serial number in Soft AP & Station modes and reported to router.
>
> From v3.70 onwards:
> - MAC as serial number in Soft AP mode
> - MAC as serial number + 1 in Station mode is reported to the router.
> Soft AP is used during onboarding and Station Mode is used once onboarded.
> (This change is due to a limitation in the ESP32 and was needed to allow for Amazon WSS
> onboarding, hence not a bug and won't be fixed in upcoming releases.)

This means that the unique ID used for LIFX bulbs no longer matches its actual MAC address, so Home Assistant is unable to correlate LIFX entities with other integrations. I noticed this because the UniFi Network integration does correlate bulbs with older firmware.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.10.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

LIFX

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/lifx/

review_comments: This sounds like something that should be handled by the library.
The library has no need to know this. It's a Home Assistant thing, because it's only needed to create connections to multiple integrations in the Device Registry.
If the library defined bulb instance has an attribute called `mac_addr` and it no longer returns a mac address, that should be fixed in the library and not in Home Assistant.
